key_insight: A trust-limited Gaussian-process surrogate can accelerate NEB calculations for small-polaron hopping while preserving DFT-level verification through controlled sampling and force limits.
engineering_relevance: This enables more practical computation of charge-transport barriers in correlated materials like TiO2, supporting faster screening of ionic/electronic migration pathways.
method: Joint energy-force Gaussian process with Matérn covariance guides NEB image updates
Active-atom RMS and max displacement trust limits trigger first-principles DFT resampling
Independent full-band DFT verification checks final pathway and barrier convergence
evidence_signal: Three independently verified 96-atom runs produced consistent barriers of 0.1637–0.1645 eV, with a final full-band maximum projected force of 0.0346 eV/Å.
watch_item: Barrier values changed in the larger 324-atom supercell, so results remain sensitive to supercell size and surrogate calibration near charge-transfer switching.
paper_title: Trust-Limited Machine-Learning-Accelerated Nudged Elastic Band Calculations for Small-Polaron Hopping in Rutile TiO2
